extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in differential geometry/geometric analysis studying Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter-level textbook material defining Perelman's reduced distance and reduced volume, proving their differential inequalities and monotonicity, deriving Jacobian comparison, and using these to state and prove a no-local-collapsing theorem for Ricci flow on (complete/compact) manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's Li–Yau type estimate (monotonicity of τH / sign of H)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the quantity H = 2Δf − |∇f|^2 + R + f/τ − n/τ (equivalently written in (2.6.8)), one has ∂(τH)/∂τ = Δ(τH) − (τH)·∇(2f) − 1/τ (τH) + nonnegative terms so that by the maximum principle max(τH) is nonincreasing as τ increases. For a fundamental solution u of the conjugate heat equation, this yields Perelman's Li–Yau type estimate (H ≤ 0 in the relevant limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differential identity and monotonicity are the analytic basis for applying the Li–Yau path integral to obtain heat-kernel type estimates for conjugate heat solutions; the text notes the limit behavior as τ→0 for fundamental solutions and that the monotonicity of τH (hence sign information on H) motivates the reduced distance construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Perelman reduced distance l(q,τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the L-length of a (space) curve γ(·) by L_τ(γ)=∫_{τ1}^{τ2} √τ (R(γ(τ),τ) + |˙γ(τ)|^2) dτ and the reduced distance l(q,τ) = (1/2√τ) inf_γ L_τ(γ) where the inf is over curves from fixed base point p at τ=0 to q at τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduced distance (called Li–Yau–Perelman distance) is the fundamental space–time distance used to define the reduced volume; the construction parallels Li–Yau's length for linear parabolic equations and underlies subsequent monotonicity formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: L-length first variation and gradient relation (Lemma 3.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: First variation formula: for a variation vector field Y along γ, δ_Y L = 2√τ⟨X,Y⟩|_{τ1}^{τ2} + ∫_{τ1}^{τ2} √τ ⟨Y, ∇_X X − 1/2 ∇R + (1/2τ) X + 2 Ric(X,·)⟩ dτ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From this one deduces that for a minimizing L-geodesic X = ˙γ, ∇L = 2√τ X and the Euler–Lagrange equation (the L-geodesic equation) follows. The formula provides boundary and bulk terms used throughout the comparison arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: L-geodesic equation (3.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth curve γ(τ) is an L-geodesic if it satisfies ∇_X X − 1/2 ∇R + (1/2τ) X + 2 Ric(X,·) = 0 where X = ˙γ(τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence: for any two spacetime points (p,0) and (q,τ) there exists an L-shortest curve satisfying this equation; this ODE and its scaled form are used to extend definitions to τ1=0 by taking limits √τ ˙γ(τ) → v as τ→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second variation and index form for L-length (Lemma 3.2.2 / Prop. 3.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Second variation formula gives δ^2_Y L = 2√τ⟨∇_X Y, Y⟩|_0^{¯τ} + ∫_0^{¯τ} √τ [2|∇_X Y|^2 + 2⟨R(Y,X)Y,X⟩ + ∇_Y ∇_Y R + 2∇_X Ric(Y,Y) − 4∇_Y Ric(Y,X)] dτ (as arranged in the text). From this one obtains the Hessian estimate along an L-shortest geodesic: Hess L(Y,Y) ≤ 1/√¯τ − 2√¯τ Ric(Y,Y) − ∫_0^{¯τ} √τ Q(X,Y) dτ (in distributional sense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q(X,Y) is the Li–Yau–Hamilton quadratic in the two-vector (X,Y). Equality holds iff Y is an L–Jacobian field (i.e., derivative of a variation of γ by L-geodesics). The index-form inequality is used to bound Hessian and Laplacian of L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laplacian bound for L and rigidity condition (Corollary 3.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary: in the sense of distributions, ΔL ≤ n / √¯τ − 2√¯τ R + (1/¯τ) K (where K = ∫_0^{¯τ} (3/2) Q(X) dτ is as defined). Moreover equality holds everywhere iff the flow is a gradient shrinking soliton satisfying Rij + (1/(2√¯τ)) ∇_i ∇_j L = (1/(2¯τ)) g_{ij}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a key elliptic-type inequality for L and supplies the rigidity criterion (gradient shrinking soliton) characterizing when inequalities are equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential inequalities for reduced distance l (Lemma 3.2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For l(q,¯τ)=L(q,¯τ)/2√¯τ one has (in distributional sense) precise identities/inequalities: formulae for ∂l/∂¯τ, |∇l|^2 (relating to L and R), and Δl bounds, collected as (3.2.11)–(3.2.13). In particular these yield ∂l/∂¯τ − Δl + |∇l|^2 − R + n/(2¯τ) ≥ 0 (equivalently ∂_¯τ − Δ + R applied to (4π¯τ)^{-n/2} e^{-l} is ≤ 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality in these inequalities characterizes gradient shrinking solitons. These inequalities are the analytic core that makes the reduced volume monotonicity proof work (they produce the key sign in the evolution of the integrand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's reduced volume (definition) and finiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the reduced volume ˜V(τ) = (4πτ)^{-n/2} ∫_M e^{-l(q,τ)} dV_τ(q) (for compact M; for complete noncompact one needs the local version). The text shows ˜V(τ) is finite (via the τ→0 asymptotics l(0)=|v|^2/4 and Jacobian behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finite Gaussian-type initial behavior (limit to Euclidean integral) is used to show well-definedness; analogy is drawn to Huisken's monotonicity for mean curvature flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of Perelman's reduced volume (Theorem 3.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reduced volume ˜V(τ) is nonincreasing in τ for solutions of the backward Ricci flow (∂_τ g_{ij} = 2R_{ij}) with bounded curvature; moreover, the monotonicity is strict unless the solution is a gradient shrinking soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof combines the pointwise differential inequality for the integrand (from Lemma 3.2.5) with integration by parts (or distributional interpretation) and the Jacobian comparison to pass to the global integral. A local version is required for noncompact complete manifolds and is important for surgery applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's Jacobian comparison theorem (Theorem 3.2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Along any shortest L-geodesic γ starting from a fixed base point, the reduced volume element (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-l(τ)} J(τ) is nonincreasing in τ (where J(τ) is the L-Jacobian of the L-exponential map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comparison of the Jacobian together with the l-evolution is the pointwise statement from which the global monotonicity of ˜V(τ) is obtained by integrating over TpM (pulling back via the L-exponential map).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of Perelman's W-functional (relation to v)
rubrics_metrics.description: v = τ H u (where u is the conjugate heat kernel density) is the integrand of Perelman's W-functional W(g,f,τ) = ∫ v dV. For compact M one has d/dτ W = −2τ ∫ |Ric + ∇^2 f − (1/(2τ)) g|^2 u dV ≤ 0 (same as Proposition 1.5.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus W is monotone nonincreasing in τ, and the integrand v and its evolution tie the analytic quantities (Ricci + Hess f − (1/2τ)g) to monotonicity; equality characterizes a shrinking soliton-type structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularized ambient metric ˜g and Ricci-flatness modulo 1/N (Proposition 3.1.1 & Corollary 3.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct ˜g on ˜M = M × S^N × R_+ by ˜g_{ij}=g_{ij}, ˜g_{αβ}=τ g_{αβ}, ˜g_{oo}=N^2/(2τ)+R, etc. The components of the curvature tensor of ˜g coincide modulo O(1/N) with the Li–Yau–Hamilton quadratic, and all components of the Ricci tensor of ˜g are O(1/N) (i.e., Ricci-flat modulo 1/N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric construction provides the intuition: for large N the ambient is approximately Ricci-flat, so Bishop–Gromov comparison heuristics applied to ˜g motivate the reduced volume monotonicity. The text uses this to give an (informal) geometric picture relating reduced volume to volume comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsed on scale r (Definition 3.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Ricci flow solution g_{ij}(t) is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on the scale r if whenever |Rm|(x,t) ≤ r^{-2} for all x in B_{t0}(x0,r) and t ∈ [t0 − r^2, t0], then Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the local noncollapsing criterion measured in terms of curvature scale; it is the notion used to quantify injectivity radius lower bounds in terms of curvature and is the statement whose uniform existence is asserted in the no-local-collapsing theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem I (Theorem 3.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any initial metric on a compact n-manifold M and the Ricci flow g_{ij}(t) on [0,T) (T<∞), there exist positive constants κ and ρ0 such that for any t0∈[0,T) and x0∈M the solution is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on all scales less than ρ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a uniform lower bound on volumes of curvature-scale-controlled balls (hence a local injectivity radius estimate) up to finite time; the theorem is proved via the monotonicity of reduced volume and scaling/contradiction arguments and is essential because it survives surgery procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic initial data for l and Jacobian as τ→0 (used for finiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For L-geodesics with limit vector v = lim_{τ→0} √τ ˙γ(τ), one has l(0) = |v|^2/4 and lim_{τ→0} (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-l(τ)} J(τ) = (4π)^{-n/2} e^{-|v|^2/4}, so integrating over TpM yields a finite Gaussian integral and shows ˜V(τ) is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These small-τ asymptotics justify the change-of-variables argument integrating over initial tangent vectors and are used in Theorem 3.2.8 to show well-definedness and finiteness of reduced volume.
